question: When moving an injured person, what is the most important goal to keep in mind?

options.A: Reaching the nearest hospital in the shortest possible time
options.B: Ensuring the patient's family members can ride along
options.C: Clearing the emergency scene before law enforcement arrives
options.D: Moving the patient safely without causing further injury

explanation: You've got this! Safety and protecting the patient from extra harm always come first, even before rushing to the hospital. Great nursing instincts!

question: Why shouldn't you rush or speed too much when transporting an accident victim?

options.A: Vehicles consume too much fuel when driven too fast
options.B: Rushing can compromise the airway or worsen existing injuries
options.C: Hospitals prefer patients to arrive slowly for administrative reasons
options.D: Rescuers get too tired to document the incident properly

explanation: Spot on! Moving too fast without control can cause dropped stretchers or mess up breathing tubes. Smooth and steady wins the race in emergency care.

question: In the emergency ABCDE assessment check, what does the letter 'B' stand for?
explanation: Easy and correct! 'B' stands for Breathing. Checking chest movement is one of the very first things we do for any emergency patient.

question: You are getting a trauma patient ready for an ambulance ride. What must you check and do FIRST?

options.A: Notifying the receiving physician of the patient's insurance status
options.B: Completing the detailed nursing admission notes
options.C: Washing and dressing all minor abrasions
options.D: Securing an open airway and controlling severe bleeding

explanation: Well done! Life-saving care always comes before paperwork or minor cuts. ABC comes first!

question: What is the best position for transporting an unconscious patient who is still breathing and has a pulse?
explanation: Brilliant! Placing them on their side (recovery position) keeps the tongue from blocking the airway and lets any fluids drain safely.

question: Why do we keep a patient with a suspected spinal injury flat on a hard board?

options.A: To make it easier to slide them into the back of an ambulance
options.B: To reduce the overall weight of the patient during lifting
options.C: To allow the nurse to check the abdomen more frequently
options.D: To prevent twisting or bending of the spinal column

explanation: Exactly right! A rigid board stops any accidental bending that could cause permanent damage to the spinal cord.

question: Which type of stretcher splits into two halves so you can slide it under a patient without rolling them?
explanation: Spot on! A scoop stretcher splits lengthwise, making it super helpful when you want to avoid rolling a fragile patient.

question: When is a basket stretcher (Stokes litter) most useful during a rescue?

options.A: For moving stable patients down smooth hospital hallways
options.B: During rough terrain, outdoor rescue operations, or hoisting
options.C: For quick transfers from a bed to a bathroom shower chair
options.D: When a patient requires immediate open-heart surgery in transit

explanation: You got it! The cage-like design protects the patient securely when navigating rough paths, stairs, or rocky areas.

question: What is the safest way to bend your body when lifting a heavy patient or equipment?
explanation: Awesome! Always lift with your legs (knees and hips bent), not your back, to protect your spine from injury.

question: Why should you avoid twisting your body while carrying a heavy load?

options.A: It causes the rescue team to lose their sense of direction
options.B: It increases the air pressure inside the transport vehicle
options.C: It automatically makes the patient slide off the stretcher
options.D: It places excessive rotational stress on the lumbar spine disks

explanation: That's correct! Twisting while carrying something heavy is one of the fastest ways nurses hurt their lower backs. Protect your spine!

question: Why is keeping a close eye on your patient so crucial while moving them in an ambulance?

options.A: Transport equipment automatically records electrical brain waves
options.B: Vehicle motion and vibrations can mask or worsen clinical changes
options.C: Hospital regulations require a full report every sixty seconds
options.D: Patients sleep better when nurses talk to them constantly

explanation: Spot on! The bumps and vibrations of a moving vehicle can hide early signs of trouble, so constant monitoring is a must.

question: While in the ambulance, you notice the intravenous (IV) line has stopped flowing. What is the very first thing you should check?

options.A: Whether the tubing is kinked or the patient's arm is bent
options.B: Whether the patient's blood type needs to be re-checked
options.C: Whether the ambulance driver is speeding too fast
options.D: Whether the hospital pharmacy has more fluid in stock

explanation: Great clinical thinking! Movement in transit often causes IV tubing to bend or kink. Always check the line physically first.

question: What do the letters in the SBAR handover tool stand for?
explanation: You nailed it! SBAR is your best friend for giving quick, structured, and clear patient updates to other healthcare workers.

question: Why is a proper verbal and written handover necessary when bringing a patient to a new ward?

options.A: To prevent family members from asking questions about the bill
options.B: To satisfy insurance companies that the trip took place
options.C: To give the transport nurse an excuse to leave the hospital early
options.D: To ensure continuity of safe care and prevent important details from being lost

explanation: Exactly! A solid handover bridges the gap between transport and the new ward, keeping patient safety front and center.
